statement: A weather station recorded the daily high temperature for $30$ days in degrees Celsius. The temperatures had a mean of $20^\circ\text{C}$ and a standard deviation of $5^\circ\text{C}$. Each temperature is converted to degrees Fahrenheit using $F = 1.8C + 32$. What is the standard deviation of the converted temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit?

choices.misconception: I thought standard deviation never changes when you convert units, so I kept 5, but multiplying by 1.8 stretches the spread.
I multiplied 5 by 1.8 squared, which is how the variance changes, not the standard deviation.
I put the standard deviation into the formula, 1.8 times 5 plus 32, but adding 32 shifts every value and does not change the spread.

hints: Think about what each part of $1.8C + 32$ does to the distances between temperatures.
Adding the same number to every value shifts the data but does not change the spread. Multiplying every value by a positive number multiplies the spread by that number.
The $+32$ leaves the standard deviation alone, and the $\times 1.8$ multiplies it by $1.8$, so compute $1.8 \times 5$.

solutions.reliable: Standard deviation measures distances from the mean. Multiplying every value by $1.8$ multiplies every distance by $1.8$, and adding $32$ to every value changes no distance. So the new standard deviation is $1.8 \times 5 = 9^\circ\text{F}$.
solutions.elegant: Two days that differ by $1^\circ\text{C}$ differ by $1.8^\circ\text{F}$, so every spread measured in degrees grows by a factor of $1.8$: $5 \times 1.8 = 9$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
